fix(renderables): a string handed to a panel, tree, column or layout draws its markup (rich-panel-gbe) (#173)

* fix(renderables): a string handed to a panel, tree, column or layout draws its markup (rich-panel-gbe)

new Panel("[bold]x[/bold]") drew the tags literally. Table cells had parsed
markup since their own fix, but panel bodies, tree labels, column items and
layout panes each built a RichText from the constructor, which does not.
The five copies of "caller content -> something to lay out" are now one,
src/renderables/embed.ts, and progress's TextColumn uses it too.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(renderables): panel titles, subtitles and rule titles draw their markup too (rich-panel-gbe)

Review of #173: a panel's title and subtitle and a rule's title are set into
a border line through inlineLabel, which parses markup, keeps a RichText's
spans, and is cut by cells. Rule takes a RichText title as Rich's does.
embed.ts no longer claims fidelity to render_str that it lacks; the console's
markup and highlight settings not reaching embedded content is
rich-markup-3sw. Every site is tested with a RichText as well as a string.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Review of #172 (CI reviewer):
- test/docs/bundle-program.ts is gone; its unit and e2e callers bundle with
  bundleExample, so the keepProcessEnv workaround has one home
- an exampleContext whose code is not indented fails instead of running empty
- barrel exports are read through resolveAlias
- `import type { X }` from the main barrel no longer stops the prelude
  importing X's value
- a throws block shows Error.prototype.toString, or `Uncaught <value>`, so an
  empty throw still shows

fix(docs): examples blame the context that threw; silent shows its note alone; ts{2} is TypeScript (rich-docs-examples-xuu.812)

Review of #172:
- a context throw is reported at the exampleContext, not the first block;
  splitRecords says whether the context finished
- the context is the chain's first scope, so it may redeclare console
- a silent block's note stands in place of output, with no empty fragments
- VitePress fence attributes ({2}, :line-numbers, [title]) no longer hide a
  TypeScript fence from every reader
- a default-plus-named import binds both names, so the prelude does not
  import the named one again
- a page runs once per docs:build, not once per VitePress build pass
- ExampleCompiler keeps parsed files by mtime, as its header claimed

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(docs): run every migrated page's examples at build time (rich-docs-examples-xuu.812)

A pre-transform Vite plugin builds each page's examples into one program
(imports hoisted, the barrel-and-console prelude, the page's exampleContext,
blocks chained in nested scopes), type-checks it under the repo's strict
options, bundles it, and runs it once under the simulated process in a 75x24
truecolor terminal. Each block's bytes are held to its marker, decoded with
decodeAnsi and encoded as a light and a dark fragment under its fence.
Every failure fails the build at the page and line.

The marker vocabulary and the fence parser are one module, which
test/docs/code-blocks.ts now reads too, so a marked block stays in the
symbol-existence sweep. Every page with a TypeScript fence starts on
NOT_YET_MIGRATED, so the site is unchanged. tscTransform moved out of
vitest.config.ts so the bundler compiles src/ the same way.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
